quotes.title: Acute Kidney Injury (AKI) and Acute Kidney Disease (AKD)
quotes.exact_continuous_quote: The draft of the KDIGO 2026 Clinical Practice Guideline for Acute Kidney Injury (AKI) and Acute Kidney Disease (AKD) was recently made available for public review. The Guideline Work Group will prepare the guideline for publication based on feedback received during the public review.

quotes.title: Acute Kidney Injury (AKI) and Acute Kidney Disease (AKD)
quotes.exact_continuous_quote: This guideline represents the first major update to the KDIGO AKI Guideline since 2012 and reflects substantial advances in the understanding, detection, and management of acute kidney injury and related disorders.

quotes.title: Consensus recommendations on the diagnosis and treatment of hyponatremia from the Austrian Society for Nephrology 2024
quotes.exact_continuous_quote: Measurement of serum-osmolality, urine osmolality and urine-sodium concentration help to diagnose the different reasons for hyponatremia. Hyponatremia induces cerebral edema and might lead to severe neurological symptoms, which need acute therapy. Also, mild forms of hyponatremia should be treated causally, or at least symptomatically. An inadequate fast increase of the serum sodium level should be avoided, because it raises the risk of cerebral osmotic demyelination.

quotes.title: UK Kidney Association Clinical Practice Guideline: Treatment of Acute Hyperkalaemia in Adults
quotes.locator: Official HTML; Lay Summary; opening paragraph
quotes.exact_continuous_quote: Hyperkalaemia may be mild (K + 5.5 – 5.9 mmol/l), moderate (K + 6.0 – 6.4 mmol/l) or severe (K + ≥ 6.5mmol/l). It can occur in the community or in hospitalised patients. Most cases of mild or moderate hyperkalaemia detected in the community can be managed without the need for hospital admission unless acutely unwell. Severe hyperkalaemia requires urgent hospital assessment as it is potentially life-threatening.

quotes.title: UK Kidney Association Clinical Practice Guideline: Treatment of Acute Hyperkalaemia in Adults
quotes.locator: Official HTML; Section II Hospital; Guideline 15.3
quotes.exact_continuous_quote: We recommend that urea and electrolytes are measured using paired lithium heparin and clotted serum samples from a large vein using gentle traction with prompt laboratory analysis if pseudo hyperkalaemia is suspected. (1A)

quotes.title: Guidelines on the management of abnormal liver blood tests
quotes.locator: PMCID PMC5754852; section s1 “Recommendations list”; Recommendation 1
quotes.exact_continuous_quote: Recommendation 1: Initial investigation for potential liver disease should include bilirubin, albumin, alanine aminotransferase (ALT), alkaline phosphatase (ALP) and γ-glutamyltransferase (GGT), together with a full blood count if not already performed within the previous 12 months. (level 2b, grade B)

quotes.title: Guidelines on the management of abnormal liver blood tests
quotes.exact_continuous_quote: Recommendation 2: Abnormal liver blood test results should only be interpreted after review of the previous results, past medical history and current medical condition. (level 5, grade D) Recommendation 3: The extent of liver blood test abnormality is not necessarily a guide to clinical significance. This is determined by the specific analyte which is abnormal (outside the reference range) and the clinical context. (level 5, grade D)

quotes.title: 2. Diagnosis and Classification of Diabetes: Standards of Care in Diabetes-2026
quotes.locator: Europe PMC core metadata; PMID 41358893; abstract sentences 1–2
quotes.exact_continuous_quote: The American Diabetes Association (ADA) "Standards of Care in Diabetes" includes the ADA's current clinical practice recommendations and is intended to provide the components of diabetes care, general treatment goals and guidelines, and tools to evaluate quality of care. Members of the ADA Professional Practice Committee for Diabetes, an interprofessional expert committee, are responsible for updating the Standards of Care annually, or more frequently as warranted.

quotes.title: WHO guideline on use of ferritin concentrations to assess iron status in individuals and populations
quotes.locator: Europe PMC core metadata; PMID 33909381; abstract sentence 1
quotes.exact_continuous_quote: This guideline provides global, evidence-informed recommendations on the use of indicators for assessing a population’s iron status and application of the use of ferritin concentrations for monitoring and evaluating iron interventions.
